newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean '97 vehicle output/exports seen rising.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean '97 vehicle output/exports seen rising.

text.p: South Korea's vehicle production is expected to rise by 6.6 percent to three million units and vehicle exports by 11.4 percent to 1.35 million units in 1997, the Korea Automobile Manufacturers' Association said on Friday.
The association said in a report last year's vehicle output grew by an estimated 11.4 percent to 2,813,800 units and exports by 23.8 percent to 1,211,900 units.
This year's domestic sales are expected to rise 3.5 percent to 1.7 million units, it said.
KAMA said this year's passenger car production was forecast to grow by 7.5 percent to 2.39 million from last year's estimated 2.22 million units.
Passenger car exports were predicted to rise by 11.7 percent to 1.18 million units from an estimated 1.06 million units in 1996, it said.

The report said South Korea's vehicle exports would be helped by a brisk world economy, longstanding sales promotions in major markets, rising demand from the Asian region and the economic recovery in East Europe.

By company, exports of Hyundai Motor Co are expected to grow by 8.8 percent to 600,000 units, those of Kia Motors Corp by 15 percent to 290,000 units and those of Daewoo Motor Co by 7.3 percent to 320,000 units, it said.
The three companies account for more than 90 percent of South Korea's vehicle exports, it said.
